title: Any hero, any place
concept: Functions · parameters, defaults and named arguments
description: Write one scene that works for every hero and place, with a mood that has a sensible default.

tasks.title: Hand a function the details
tasks.body: def greet(name): gives the function a parameter: a name for a value it is handed. greet("Nova") calls it with the argument "Nova", so inside the function, name holds "Nova".
tasks.detail: A function can take several parameters, matched in order: def trade(item, price):. A default, as in def trade(item, price=5):, is used when a call leaves that value out. A call can also name them, trade(price=2, item="rope"), and then their order does not matter.

tasks.code:
# One scene, many heroes
def arrive(hero, place="the harbour"):
    print(hero + " arrives at " + place + ".")

arrive("Nova")
arrive("Kai", "the tower")
arrive(place="the mill", hero="Ada")
tasks.output:
Nova arrives at the harbour.
Kai arrives at the tower.
Ada arrives at the mill.
tasks.note: The first call leaves place out, so it uses the default. The second matches its arguments in order. The third names them, so they can come in any order.

tasks.question: What would arrive("the tower", "Kai") print?
tasks.why: Arguments without names are matched in order: the first one becomes hero, whatever it says.

tasks.prompt: Predict, then run: swap the two arguments in the second call. Then give hero a default too, and call arrive() with no arguments at all.

Write a function called scene(hero, place, mood="calm") that prints one line: the hero, the words is in, the place, a comma, the word feeling, and the mood, ending with a full stop. For example, scene("Nova", "the cave") prints Nova is in the cave, feeling calm. Your program should not ask for input: the check calls your functions with its own values.
hints: The def line lists three parameters, and the last one has a default: mood="calm".
Inside, build the line from the parameters, not from any one hero's name, so that every call gets its own hero and place.
The same idea with other names: def order(dish, drink="water"): can print dish + " with " + drink + "." for any dish.

error_hints.text: Check the def line: scene() takes the hero, the place and then the mood, and the mood has a default so calls may leave it out.
Inside the function, use the parameter names from the def line, spelled the same way.
With scene("Nova", "the cave") the line is Nova is in the cave, feeling calm. Check the spaces, the comma and the full stop.
A mood given in the call replaces the default: scene("Kai", "the market", "brave") feels brave.
A call can name the mood, mood="sleepy". The parameter must be called mood for that to work.
Check another hero and place: the line must come from the parameters, never from a name written into the function.
Check a call that names every argument: the parameters must be called hero, place and mood.

similar_example.code:
def order(dish, drink="water"):
    print(dish + " with " + drink + ".")

order("soup")
order("pie", "milk")
similar_example.note: A meal order with a default drink. Your scene() has two parameters before its default, and different words around them.

other_ways.code:
def scene(hero, place, mood="calm"):
    print(f"{hero} is in {place}, feeling {mood}.")
other_ways.note: An f-string puts each value straight into the sentence, with no + signs.
join() puts a space between the pieces of a list. Useful when a sentence is built from many parts.

cases.expected: Nova is in the cave, feeling calm.
Kai is in the market, feeling brave.
Ada is in the mill, feeling sleepy.
Bo is in a boat, feeling calm.
Lin is in the woods, feeling lost.
